main_finding: Rice paddies supported hygrophilous and wetland-associated orthopterans and functioned as surrogate wetland habitat
key_limitation: Does not quantify response to specific flooding-duration changes

main_finding: Rice fields and supply canal hosted distinct aquatic primary-producer communities under strongly fluctuating wetland-like conditions including sporadic drought
key_limitation: Two rice fields only and no long-term hydroperiod-response estimate

main_finding: Rice fields functioned as managed temporary wetlands and supported diverse macroinvertebrate assemblages including rare species; water permanence was one of several community drivers
key_limitation: Management and water permanence were not isolated as single causal factors

main_finding: Italian rice paddies provide temporary aquatic habitat and may partly substitute for lost lowland wetlands while biodiversity responses vary among taxa and management conditions
key_limitation: Review synthesizes heterogeneous evidence and provides no universal hydroperiod threshold

study_location: Mediterranean region including Italian rice systems
main_finding: Rice fields can substitute partly for natural wetlands as feeding habitat for waterbirds in Mediterranean landscapes
key_limitation: Older agricultural context and focused on birds rather than whole-community biodiversity
